snippet.title: The Secret to a Sustainable Health Journey
snippet.description:
This week’s conversation with Julie Rice is about the ways building community can help sustain a healthy life — not a goal weight, but a life. After turning SoulCycle into a cultural phenomenon, Julie co-founded Peoplehood around the idea that human connection is a profound practice; it’s also at the forefront of how she is reshaping the Weight Watchers experience. Julie opens up about her own health and career trajectory, her changing relationship to her body, and why connection should be at the heart of wellness conversations.

snippet.title: Dressing a Changing Body
snippet.description:
Nobody talks about how emotionally weird it is to dress a body that's changing. The closet purges. The grief of giving away clothes you loved. The dressing room moments that catch you off guard. Whether to dress the body you have or the one you imagine is in your future. In this episode, Samhita Mukhopadhyay talks with celebrity stylist, creative director, and author Erin Walsh about style as identity when your identity is in flux, and the psychology of body image underneath it all.

Guest: Erin Walsh

snippet.title: Growing Up on Screen in a Bigger Body
snippet.description:
Raven Goodwin has been navigating weight and body image in public since she was a child actress. At 18 she starred in Huge, a show about teenagers at a weight-loss camp. Now she's a WW cover star, a mother, and a woman whose relationship to her body has played out on screen for two decades. This conversation is about what it's like when Hollywood has opinions about your body before you've even formed your own — and what it means to come full circle.

snippet.title: Hacked Hunger and the Role of GLP-1s
snippet.description:
What happened to our food, our bodies, and our ability to stop eating — and who's responsible? Writer and journalist Johann Hari tracked down the scientists who discovered GLP-1, and traveled the world investigating the food system that was engineered to override our satiety signals. Here, Hari discusses his personal journey on a GLP-1—from losing food as a coping mechanism to embracing self-compassion in a world that says weight loss should involve punishment.

Guest: Johann Hari

snippet.title: Shame, Stigma, and Saying It Out Loud
snippet.description:
Some things you only say to your best friend. This time, Susie Banikarim — Emmy-winning journalist, podcast host, and one of Samhita's closest friends — is saying them out loud.

The shame she has felt for being overweight, wanting to lose weight, and being on a GLP-1 (and still not being thin). How women privately support each other and share information about these medications. Intentional weight loss as a dirty word.

And Susie's radical declaration: she doesn't care about being thin or what people think about her journey anymore.

Guest: Susie Banikarim
